function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a big chain, or a fully‑online experience: | Category | What to Look For | Why It Might Be Right for You | |----------|------------------|------------------------------| | **Local Bakeries** | • Small‑batch, artisanal shops
• Custom designs & seasonal flavors
• Often have a “pick‑up” option | Great for supporting your community, getting fresh ingredients, and having a personal touch. | | **National Chains** | • Famous names like Magnolia Bakery, Sprinkles, or Mrs. Fields
• Consistent quality across locations
• Usually offer a wide menu of ready‑made and custom cakes | Ideal if you want a brand you know, or if you’re traveling and need a reliable place. | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | • Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, Instacart, Amazon Fresh
• Many partner with local bakeries and national chains alike | Convenient if you don’t want to leave the house; they’ll bring it right to your doorstep. | | **Specialty Dessert Shops** | • Chocolate‑focused places like Jacques Torres, La Maison du Chocolat
• Vegan or gluten‑free specialists
• Boutique pastry chefs | Perfect if you’re after a niche flavor profile or dietary restriction. | | **DIY Kits & Meal‑Prep Services** | • Blue Apron, HelloFresh, or local meal‑prep companies that include dessert kits
• Pre‑measured ingredients & step‑by‑step instructions | Fun if you enjoy baking yourself but still want a professional finish. | ### How to Choose 1. **Know Your Flavor & Size Needs** * Do you want a classic vanilla layer, a decadent chocolate ganache, or something exotic like matcha or salted caramel? * Estimate how many people you’re feeding to pick the right size. 2. **Check Reviews & Ratings** * On Google Maps, Yelp, or the platform’s own rating system. * Look for photos of finished cakes—this gives you a sense of design quality. 3. **Delivery Time & Availability** * Some bakeries only deliver on certain days or within a limited radius. * Online platforms often show real‑time availability and estimated arrival windows. 4. **Customization Options** * Local shops usually let you choose frosting, fillings, and decorations. * National chains may have pre‑designed themes (e.g., Disney, Harry Potter). 5. **Budget** * Prices vary widely: $20–$30 for a small birthday cake, $50–$100+ for larger or highly customized orders. * Don’t forget delivery fees—some platforms waive them for orders over a certain amount. ### Quick Tips * **Order Early** – Especially for custom cakes or holiday specials, you might need 1–2 weeks’ notice. * **Ask About Allergens** – If someone has dietary restrictions, confirm that the bakery uses separate equipment or can accommodate. * **Confirm Pickup vs. Delivery** – Pick‑up saves on delivery costs and lets you inspect the cake before leaving the shop. --- #### Need a Recommendation for Your Area? If you tell me your city or zip code, I can suggest a few top-rated local bakeries or popular chains that deliver there. Or, if you prefer a nationwide brand, I can point you toward their nearest store or online ordering portal. Let me know what works best for you!
